understanding the mass. the offertory: "blessed are you, lord god of all creation" what the priest is doing the liturgy of the word is complete. now the altar is prepared, gifts are brought forward, and the mass moves into its second great movement - the liturgy of the eucharist. the priest receives bread and wine, lifts each slightly, and offers quiet prayers of blessing drawn from ancient jewish table prayers. he says these prayers in a quiet voice, or even silently. these are humble gifts, bread and wine, fruit of the earth, work of human hands. but that ordinariness is precisely the point. god does not ask for the extraordinary. he takes what we bring and transforms it entirely. how we should respond the collection taken up at this moment is not an interruption, it belongs here. money represents our labour, our time, our life. placing it in the bags is a small but genuine act of offering ourselves alongside the bread and wine. as the gifts are brought forward, make an interior offering of your own. whatever you are carrying this week work, worry, joy, grief - place it consciously on that altar alongside the bread and wine. living this at mass the offertory is easily overlooked as a moment of transition. reclaim it. when the priest lifts the bread, lift something of yourself with it. pope leoxiv prayer for the recovery of pope leo. loving and merciful god, we pray for our holy father, pope leo, asking you to bless him with healing, strength, and renewed health. be close to him in his time of need, grant him peace and comfort, and guide those who care for him. may he experience your loving presence and be restored to good health, so that he may continue to shepherd your church with wisdom and love. amen. masses 10 am monday to saturday, vigil mass saturday 6.30 pm sunday masses 9 am, 10.30 am, 12 noon . confessions after 10 am mass on saturday and on request baptisms on the 2nd saturday of each month at 2 pm. please contact the parish office contacts parish office 8316016 fr michael o’grady
